scope: Every protein that would be a Target candidate while its rare-cell signal is dismissed, or after release from the pooled 1% detection flag.

rubric.R1: A primary source reports the human gene in a panel organ by a gene-specific assay, and donor-level single-cell data detect it in that organ in at least 1% of one donor population. The rare-cell grade becomes established.
rubric.R2: A primary source reports the human gene, RNA or protein, by a gene-specific assay in normal adult tissue that the hazard registry tiers Vital or Protected, and no gene-specific multi-tissue panel or reliable IHC contradicts it. Unsafe.
rubric.R3: Human loss of function causes disease of a Vital tissue, and the ortholog is expressed in that adult tissue. Unsafe.
rubric.none: No publication, restriction to germline, placenta or embryo, conflicting reports, assays shared with paralogs, cultured or diseased samples, other species alone, or database annotation alone. Recorded; no category effect.

method: Web literature search by Claude subagents on 2026-11-10; each claim carries the URL opened and the quote returned.
limitations: Many pages were read through a fetch tool that summarizes, so quotes are as that tool relayed them
Several papers were read at abstract level because full text was blocked; each evidence item says so
PubMed was reached through Europe PMC or E-utilities
A null result means nothing was found in this search, not that nothing exists
HPA and GTEx bulk values are numeric filters elsewhere and were not counted as literature

entries.reported_tissue: brain (low-level RNA; disputed)
entries.summary: Morgan et al. 2013 (full text opened, PMC3581823) reported MAGE-A12 RNA in normal human brain by three methods (qRT-PCR with sequencing of products on commercial pooled total-brain and cerebellum RNA and on autopsy brain regions of patients 5 and 8; NanoString on commercial neurological RNAs; RNA-seq of frontal cortex from 6 controls) and rare neurons staining with a pan-MAGE-A antibody (6C1) that cannot identify MAGE-A12; they proposed MAGE-A12 in a subset of neurons as the cause of fatal neurotoxicity. Martin et al. 2020 (PMC7946352) dispute this: GTEx brain maximum 0.3 TPM, no MAGE-A12 RNA above negative-control probe by BaseScope ISH in 8 postmortem brains, the IHC criticized as uncontrolled, and an EPS8L2 peptide proposed instead, while conceding MAGE-A12 cannot be excluded. Classical RT-PCR surveys (De Plaen 1994; UniProt) describe MAGE genes as silent in healthy tissues except testis/placenta.
entries.decision_reason: Sequenced qRT-PCR products in normal brain (Morgan 2013); our donor-level data detect it in brain. A later in situ study found no signal and proposed another peptide, and concedes MAGE-A12 cannot be excluded.

evidence.tissue: Commercial normal human total brain and cerebellum RNA (pools of 23 and 11 donors); also 11 autopsy brain regions each from trial patients 5 and 8

evidence.quote: These results demonstrated that the MAGE -A9 and MAGE-A12 transcripts were amplified from these normal human brain samples.
evidence.limitations: Very low copy numbers; pooled commercial RNA. Authors themselves note for the autopsy samples 'the potential for contamination of normal brain tissue from these patients' tumors'. Copy-number values were relayed by the fetch tool from tables, not quoted.

evidence.assay: BaseScope RNA in situ hybridization (ACD) on FFPE sections; GTEx/HPA/FANTOM5 database analysis

evidence.quote: No expression of MAGE-A12 was observed above the detection limit determined by the negative-control probe.
evidence.limitations: Authors (employees of a TCR-therapy company) concede: 'it remains possible that despite a thorough search we missed rare MAGE-A12-expressing cells' and RNA instability in FFPE; EPS8L2 is called 'a likely but still unproven source'.

Conversely, Barger et al. 2018 state from GTEx RNA-seq that Group 3 POTE-actin genes (which include POTEF) show widespread normal-tissue expression and are not testis-specific; that is bulk RNA-seq subject to the same paralog (and actin) cross-mapping concern. entries.decision_reason: Reports conflict, cannot separate the gene from paralogs, or come from cultured, diseased or fetal samples.

HPA (antibody HPA046327, Supported, but 'target protein from more than one gene') reports only trophoblast staining; a 2024 paper shows the antisense lncRNA PSG8-AS1 is oligodendrocyte-expressed in human brain, which is relevant to interpreting brain reads at this locus.
entries.decision_reason: Reports conflict, cannot separate the gene from paralogs, or come from cultured, diseased or fetal samples.

HPA instead classifies RNA as testis-enriched with no normal-tissue protein estimate.

entries.summary: No primary paper with a gene-specific assay of TDRD15 across normal adult human tissues was found. The only functional study (golden hamster knockout) reports testis-restricted expression, and HPA RNA is testis enriched, but HPA's mass-spectrometry summary lists protein as group enriched in heart muscle and lung (one donor, no values shown) and a skin-swab proteomics study lists TDRD15 as upregulated in atopic dermatitis skin. These protein-level hints are unvalidated and conflict with the RNA picture.
entries.decision_reason: Reports conflict, cannot separate the gene from paralogs, or come from cultured, diseased or fetal samples.

entries.summary: Primary sources consistently describe TPTE as testis-restricted: Northern blot 'exclusively expressed in the testis' (Chen 1999), RT-PCR on normal tissue cDNA panels positive in testis only (Dong 2003), protein in spermatocytes/prespermatids (Tapparel 2003), and HPA IHC (HPA049690, Enhanced) showing only spermatocyte staining. Caveats: TPTE has highly homologous copies (TPTE2/TPIP and others) that older assays may not separate, and the Dong 2003 figure legend mentions 'normal pancreas', inconsistent with its own text.
entries.decision_reason: Sources describe germline, placental or embryonic restriction, or did not test adult somatic tissue.

entries.toxicity_reports: TPTE is one of four antigens in the BNT111 (FixVac) mRNA melanoma vaccine. BioNTech's press release on the Lipo-MERIT phase 1 Nature paper states: 'Overall, BNT111 treatment was well tolerated with no dose limiting toxicity. Most common adverse events were mild to moderate, transient flu-like symptoms, such as pyrexia and chills.' (https://www.biontech.com/us/en/home/mediaroom/news/press-releases/2020/07/biontech-publishes-data-mrna-based-bnt111-fixvac-melanoma-trial.html). This is a company summary; I did not open the Nature paper's adverse-event tables. No TPTE-attributed on-target toxicity report was found.

entries.summary: No human gene-specific assay showing TRIM60 in normal adult vital tissue was found. entries.summary: Feng et al. 2016 (NEJM) measured all beta-tubulin isotypes by qRT-PCR and report TUBB8 as unique to oocytes and early embryos and essentially absent in mature sperm and in somatic tissues such as brain and liver; UniProt cites this paper. One caution: the HPA page lists a mass-spectrometry tissue-specificity label 'Group enriched (Bone marrow, Cerebral cortex, Fallopian tube, Ovary)' and its IHC antibodies are rated Uncertain because they target protein from more than one gene, so HPA protein-level data cannot be attributed to TUBB8 versus other beta-tubulins/TUBB8B and does not meet the Enhanced/Supported bar.
entries.decision_reason: Sources describe germline, placental or embryonic restriction, or did not test adult somatic tissue.
